zh: 第三天下午，七姑奶奶陪了罗四姐去请教吴铁口。他住的二马路，英文名字叫做Rope Walk Road，翻译出来是“纤道路”，当初洋泾浜还可以通船，不过水浅要拉纤，这条纤路改成马路，就叫纤道路。本地人叫不来英文路名，就拿首先开辟的Garden Lane叫做大马路，往南第二条便叫二马路，以下三马路、四马路、五马路，一直到洋泾浜，都是东西向。前两年大马路改名南京路，二马路改名杭州路，有人跟洋人说，南京到杭州的水路是两条，一条长江，一条运河，南京是长江下游，要挑个长江上游的大码头当路名，跟南京路才连得起来，因而改为九江路，三马路也就是“海关路”，自然成为汉口路。不过上海人叫惯了，仍旧称做大马路、二马路。
en: On the afternoon of the third day, the Seventh Lady accompanied Luo Sijie to consult Wu Tiekou. He lived on Second Road, whose English name had been Rope Walk Road, translated into Chinese as Towpath Road. In the early days, boats could still use Yangjing Creek, but the shallow water made towing necessary. When the towpath was turned into a road, it retained that name. The local people could not manage the English street names, so they called Garden Lane, the first road opened, First Road. The next to the south became Second Road, followed by Third, Fourth and Fifth Roads, all running east and west, down to Yangjing Creek. Two years earlier, First Road had been renamed Nanjing Road and Second Road Hangzhou Road. Someone pointed out to the foreigners that there were two waterways between Nanjing and Hangzhou, the Yangtze and the Grand Canal. Since Nanjing was on the lower Yangtze, the name of a major port farther upstream would make a more fitting companion to Nanjing Road. Second Road was therefore renamed Jiujiang Road, and Third Road, formerly Customs Road, naturally became Hankou Road. Shanghai people were accustomed to the old names, however, and continued to say First Road and Second Road.

zh: 二马路开辟得早，市面早就繁华了。吴铁口“候教”之处在二马路富厚里，进弄堂右首第一家就是，二座石库房子打通，客堂很大，上面挂满了达官巨商名流送的匾额，胡雪岩也送了一块，题的是“子平绝诣”四字，挂在北面板壁上，板壁旁边有一道门，里面就是吴铁口设砚之处。那吴铁口生得方面大耳，两撇八字胡子，年纪只有三十出头，不过戴了一副大墨晶眼镜，看上去比较老气，身上穿的是枣红缎子夹袍，外套玄色团花马褂，头上青缎小帽，帽檐上镶一块极大的玭霞，手上留着极长的指甲，左手大拇指上套一个汉玉扳指，右手无名指上还有一枚方钻白金戒指，马褂上又是黄澄澄横过胸前的一条金表链，打扮得象个花花公子。“古太太，”吴铁口起身迎接，马褂下面垂着四个大小荷包，他摘下眼镜笑道：“你的气色真好。”“交比劫运了，怎么不好。”七姑奶奶指着罗四姐说：“这位是我的要好姐妹，姓罗。吴先生，你叫她罗四姐好了。”“是，是！罗四姐。两位请坐。”红木书桌旁边，有两张凳子，一张在对面，一张在左首，七姑奶奶自己坐了对面，示意罗四姐坐在吴铁口身旁，以便交谈。吴铁口重新戴上墨晶眼镜，在那张红木太师椅上落坐，挽起衣袖，提笔在手，问明罗四姐的年月日时，在水牌上将她的“四柱”排了出来：“已巳、辛未、甲子、甲子”，然后批批点点，搁笔凝神细看。
en: Second Road had been opened early, and its shops and businesses had long flourished. Wu Tiekou's place for receiving clients was in Fuhou Lane: the first house on the right. Two stone-gated houses had been joined together, making a large reception hall. Its walls were covered with inscribed plaques presented by high officials, wealthy merchants and distinguished men. Hu Xueyan had given one himself, bearing the words “Supreme Mastery of Ziping Astrology.” It hung on the north partition, beside a door leading to Wu's consulting room. Wu had a square face, large ears and a moustache that spread down on either side. He was only a little over thirty, but his large dark-crystal spectacles made him look older. He wore a lined robe of date-red satin beneath a black jacket patterned with round floral medallions. An enormous stone called pinxia was set in the band of his blue-satin cap. His fingernails were very long. On his left thumb he wore an archer's ring of Han jade, on his right ring finger a platinum ring set with a square diamond; a bright gold watch chain crossed his chest. He was dressed like a fashionable rake. “Mrs Gu!” He rose to greet them, four purses of different sizes dangling beneath his jacket. Removing his spectacles, he smiled. “How well you look.” “With a bijie period like this, how could I not?” She indicated Luo. “This is a dear friend of mine, surnamed Luo. You may call her Sister Luo.” “Certainly. Sister Luo. Please sit down, both of you.” There were two stools beside the rosewood desk, one opposite Wu and one to his left. The Seventh Lady took the former, indicating that Luo should sit beside him for ease of conversation. Wu put on his spectacles, settled into his rosewood armchair, rolled back his sleeves and took up his brush. Having asked Luo's birth year, month, day and hour, he wrote her Four Pillars on a writing tablet: ji-si, xin-wei, jia-zi, jia-zi. He added marks and annotations, laid down the brush and studied them intently.

zh: 这一看，足足看了一刻钟，罗四姐从侧面望去，只见他墨晶镜片后面的眼珠，眨得很厉害，心里不由得有些发毛。“吴先生，”她终于忍不住了，“我的命不好？”吴铁口摘下眼镜，看着罗四姐说：“可惜了！”接着望对面的七姑奶奶，加重语气说：“真可惜！”“怎么？”七姑奶奶说：“吴先生，请你实说。君子问祸不问福，罗四姐很开通的，你用不着有啥忌讳。”吴铁口重重点一点头，将眼镜放在一边，拿笔指点着说。“罗四姐，你是木命，‘日元’应下一个‘正印’，时辰上又是甲子，木‘比’‘印’庇，光看日时两柱，就是个逢凶化吉、遇难成祥的‘上造’。”罗四姐不懂什么叫“上造”，但听得出命是好命，当即说道：“吴先生，请你再说下去。”“木命生在夏天，又是已火之年，这株树本来很难活，好得有子水滋润，不但可活，而且是株大树。金木水火土，五行俱备，‘财’、‘官’、‘印’、‘食’四字全，又是正官正印，这个八字，如果是男命，就同苏州的潘文荣公一样，状元宰相，寿高八十，儿孙满堂，荣华富贵享不尽。可惜是女命！”
en: He studied them for a full quarter of an hour. From the side, Luo could see his eyes blinking rapidly behind the dark lenses, and she began to feel uneasy. “Mr Wu,” she said at last, unable to contain herself, “is my destiny bad?” He removed his spectacles and looked at her. “What a pity!” Then he turned to the Seventh Lady and repeated with emphasis, “A very great pity!” “What is it? Please tell us frankly. A sensible person asks about misfortune, not good fortune. Sister Luo is broad-minded. There is no need to spare her feelings.” Wu nodded heavily, set his spectacles aside and pointed with his brush. “Sister Luo, yours is a Wood destiny. Beneath your day stem lies a Direct Seal, and the hour is also jia-zi: Wood has a fellow to support it and a Seal to shelter it. Judging by the day and hour pillars alone, this is a superior configuration, one that turns misfortune into blessing and danger into good luck.” Luo did not understand “superior configuration,” but she could tell that her destiny was good. “Please go on.” “Wood born in summer, in a si-Fire year as well: this tree would normally find it hard to survive. Fortunately, zi-Water nourishes it. Not only can it live; it is a great tree. Metal, Wood, Water, Fire and Earth are all present, and so are Wealth, Officer, Seal and the Food God. Moreover, these are a Direct Officer and a Direct Seal. If this were a man's horoscope, he would be like Lord Pan Wenrong of Suzhou: first in the imperial examination, a chief minister, living to eighty with children and grandchildren all around him, enjoying endless honour and riches. A pity it is a woman's destiny!”

zh: 罗四姐尚未开口，七姑奶奶抗声说道：“女命又怎么样？状元宰相还不是女人生的？”“古太太，你不要光火！”吴铁口从从容容地答道：“我说可惜，不是说罗四姐的命不好。这样的八字如果再说不好，天理难容了。”听这一说，七姑奶奶才回嗔作喜，“那么，可惜在哪里呢，吴先生，”她说：“千万请你实说。”“我本来要就命论命，实话直说的，现在倒不敢说了。”“为啥呢？”“古太太火气这么大，万一我说了不中听的话，古太太一个耳光劈上来，我这个台坍不起。”“对不住，对不住！”七姑奶奶笑道道歉，“吴先生，请你放心。话说明白了，我自然不会光火。”说完，吴铁口叫小跟班拿水烟袋来吸水烟，又叫小跟班装果盘招待堂客。七姑奶奶一面连声：“不客气，不客气。”一面却又唤小大姐取来她的银水烟袋，点上纸媒，好整以暇地也“呼噜呼噜”地吸将起来。她跟吴铁口取得极深的默契而扮演的这出双簧，已将罗四姐迷惑住了，渴望想听“可惜”些什么，见此光景，心里焦急，而且有些侄七姑奶奶不体谅她的心事，却又不便实说，只好假装咳嗽，表示为水烟的烟子呛着了，借以暗示七姑奶奶可以歇手了。
en: Before Luo could speak, the Seventh Lady protested loudly. “What is wrong with a woman's destiny? Are examination champions and chief ministers not born of women?” “Do not be angry, Mrs Gu,” Wu replied calmly. “When I say it is a pity, I do not mean that Sister Luo's destiny is bad. Heaven would not forgive me if I called a horoscope like this bad.” Her anger gave way to pleasure. “Then what is there to regret? Please, Mr Wu, tell us honestly.” “I had intended to judge the horoscope on its merits and speak plainly. Now I hardly dare.” “Why not?” “With your temper, Mrs Gu, if I said something unwelcome, you might slap me. I could not afford such a loss of dignity.” “I beg your pardon!” She laughed apologetically. “Rest assured. Explain yourself clearly, and of course I shan't lose my temper.” Wu called for his water pipe, then told his young attendant to bring a fruit platter for the ladies. Repeatedly protesting against all this trouble, the Seventh Lady nevertheless summoned her maid to bring her silver water pipe. She lit a paper spill and began smoking with leisurely, bubbling draws. She and Wu were playing their duet with a perfect understanding, and Luo was already taken in. Desperate to learn what was so regrettable, she grew impatient at this interruption, even resenting the Seventh Lady's failure to consider her anxiety. Unable to say so openly, she pretended to cough, as though the pipe smoke were choking her, to hint that her friend might stop.

zh: “把窗户开开。”吴铁口将水烟袋放下，重新提笔，先看七姑奶奶，将她的注意力吸引过来，方始开口说道：“女命跟男命的看法不同，女命以‘克我’为‘夫星’，所以男命的‘正官’、‘偏官’，在女命中都当丈夫来看。这是一句‘总经’，要懂这个道理，才晓得罗四姐的八字，为啥可惜？“七姑奶奶略通命理，听得懂他的话，罗四姐不十分了了，但为急于听下文，也微微颔首，表示会意。“金克木，月上的这个‘辛金’，就是‘甲木’的夫星。坏就坏在时辰上也有个甲，这有个名堂，叫做‘二女争夫’。”七姑奶奶与罗四姐不约而同地互看了一眼，罗四姐有所示意，七姑奶奶也领会，便代她发言。“吴先生，你是说另外有个女人，跟罗四姐争？”“不错。”“那么争得过，争不过呢？”“急得过就不可惜了。”吴铁口说：“二女争夫，强者为胜。照表面看，你是甲子，我也是甲子，子水生甲木，好比小孩打架，这面大人出来帮儿子，那面也有大人出来说话，旗鼓相当扯个直。”“嗯，嗯，”罗四姐这下心领神会，连连说道：“我懂了，我懂了。”“罗四姐，照规矩说，时上的甲子本来争不过你的，为啥呢，你的夫星紧靠在你，近水楼台先得月，应该你占上风。可惜‘庚子望未’，辰戌丑未‘四季土’，土生金，对方就是‘财星官’，对夫星倒是大吉大利，对你大坏，坏在‘财损印’！好比小孩子打架，一方面有父母，一方面父母不在了，是个孤儿。你想，打得过人家，打不过人家？”
en: “Open the window,” Wu ordered. He put down his pipe and took up his brush again, first looking at the Seventh Lady to secure her attention. “A woman's horoscope must be read differently from a man's. In a woman's destiny, the element that controls her represents the Husband Star. Thus what we call the Direct Officer and Indirect Officer in a man's horoscope both stand for husbands in a woman's. That is a fundamental rule. You must understand it to see why Sister Luo's horoscope is regrettable.” The Seventh Lady knew something of astrology and followed him. Luo understood less, but, eager for what came next, nodded faintly too. “Metal controls Wood. This xin-Metal in the month pillar is the Husband Star for jia-Wood. The trouble is that there is another jia in the hour pillar. We have a name for that: Two Women Contending for One Husband.” The women exchanged a simultaneous glance. Luo's look conveyed a request, and the Seventh Lady spoke for her. “You mean another woman will compete with Sister Luo?” “Exactly.” “Can she win?” “If she could, there would be nothing to regret. When two women contend for one husband, the stronger wins. On the surface, each is jia-zi, with zi-Water generating jia-Wood. It is like children fighting: a parent comes out to help the child on one side, and another parent speaks up on the other. They seem evenly matched.” “Yes, yes, I understand!” Luo said repeatedly. “By the usual rule, Sister Luo, the jia-zi in the hour pillar ought not to beat you. Your Husband Star is right beside you: the pavilion nearest the water catches the moon first. You should have the advantage. Unfortunately, there is the configuration called geng-zi wang-wei. Chen, xu, chou and wei are the Earth of the four seasons, and Earth generates Metal. On the other side, Wealth benefits the Officer. That is excellent for the Husband Star but disastrous for you, because Wealth Damages the Seal. Imagine children fighting when one has parents and the other has lost theirs and is an orphan. Could the orphan defeat the other child?”

zh: 这番解说，听得懂的七姑奶奶觉得妙不可言：“吴先生，我看看。”吴铁口将水牌倒了过来，微侧着向罗四姐这面，让她们都能得见，七姑奶奶细看了一会，指点着向罗四姐说：“你看，庚下这个未，是土，紧靠着你的那个子，是水，水克土。水是财，土是印，所以叫做财损印。没有办法，你命中注定，争不过人家。”“争不过人家，怎么样呢？”罗四姐问。这话当然要吴铁口来回答：“做小！”两字斩钉截铁。罗四姐听他语声冷酷无情，大起反感，提高了声音说：“不愿意做小呢！”“克夫。”“克过了。”“还是要做小！”“偏要做大！”“做大还是要克，嫁一个克一个。”罗四姐脸都气白了，“我倒不相信……”一个铁口，一个硬碰，看看要吵架了，七姑奶奶赶紧拉一拉罗四姐的衣服说：“宁可同爷强，不可同命强，你先听吴先生说，说得没有道理再驳也不迟。”“我如果说得没有道理，古太太，罗四姐请我吃耳光不还手。”吴铁口指着水牌说：“罗四姐克过了，八字上也看得出来的，‘印’是荫覆，在家从父，出嫁从夫，这印是个靠山，丈夫去世，不就是靠山倒了？”说着，抬眼去看。
en: The Seventh Lady, who could follow the explanation, thought it marvellous. “Let me look, Mr Wu.” He turned the tablet round, angling it slightly towards Luo so that both could see. After studying it, the Seventh Lady pointed things out to her friend. “Look. This wei beneath geng is Earth. It is right beside your zi, which is Water, and Water controls Earth. Water is Wealth and Earth is the Seal, hence Wealth Damages the Seal. There is nothing to be done. You are destined to lose to the other woman.” “And what happens if I lose?” That, of course, was for Wu to answer. “Become a concubine.” The words were uncompromising. Repelled by his cold, unfeeling tone, Luo raised her voice. “And if I refuse to become a concubine?” “You will bring death to your husband.” “I have already lost one.” “You must still become a concubine.” “I insist on being a principal wife!” “Then you will still bring death. Every man you marry will die.” Luo's face went white with anger. “I don't believe…” Wu's iron certainty met an equally unyielding resistance. Seeing a quarrel about to break out, the Seventh Lady quickly tugged Luo's clothes. “Better defy your father than defy your fate. Hear Mr Wu out. If he makes no sense, there will be time enough to contradict him.” “If I make no sense, Mrs Gu, Sister Luo may slap me and I shall not lift a hand.” Wu pointed to the tablet. “Her husband's death can also be seen here. The Seal represents shelter. At home a woman depends on her father; once married, on her husband. The Seal is her support. If her husband dies, has that support not collapsed?” He raised his eyes to observe her reaction.

zh: 罗四姐脸色比较缓和了，七姑奶奶便说：“为啥还是要做小呢？”“因为未土克了第一个子水，过去就克第二个子水了，逃不掉的。真的不肯做小，也没有办法，所谓‘人各有志，不能相强。’不过，这一来，前面的‘财’、‘官’、‘食’就不必再看了。”“为啥不必再看？”“人都不在了，看它何用？”罗四姐大吃一惊，“吴先生，”她问，“你说不肯做小，命就没有了？”“当然。未土连克子水，甲木不避，要跟它硬上，好，木克土，甲木有帮手，力量很强，不过你们倒看看未土，年上那个己土是帮手，这还在其次，最厉害是已火，火生土，源源不绝，请问哪方面强？五行生克，向来克不倒就要被克。这块未土硬得象块石头一样，草木不生，甲木要去斗它，就好比拿木头去开山，木头敲断，山还是山。”听得这番解说。罗四姐象斗败了的公鸡似地，刚才那种“偏要做大”的倔强之气，消失得无影无踪，但心里却仍不甘做小。
en: Luo's expression had softened somewhat. The Seventh Lady asked, “But why must she still become a concubine?” “Because after wei-Earth has overcome the first zi-Water, it goes on to overcome the second. There is no escaping it. If she truly refuses to become a concubine, there is nothing to be done. Everyone has their own aspirations; we cannot force them. But then there is no need to examine the Wealth, Officer and Food God in the earlier part of the horoscope.” “Why not?” “What use are they if the person is no longer alive?” Luo was badly startled. “Mr Wu, do you mean I shall die if I refuse to become a concubine?” “Certainly. Wei-Earth overcomes one zi-Water after another. Suppose jia-Wood refuses to retreat and confronts it. Very well: Wood controls Earth, and jia-Wood has assistance, so its strength is considerable. But look at wei-Earth. The ji-Earth in the year pillar supports it. That is not even the most important thing: the greatest power is si-Fire, for Fire generates Earth, supplying it without end. Which side is stronger? In the interaction of the Five Elements, what fails to overcome its opponent is overcome in turn. This wei-Earth is hard as rock, on which nothing can grow. If jia-Wood challenges it, it is like trying to split a mountain with a piece of timber. The timber breaks; the mountain remains.” Luo looked like a defeated fighting cock. Her fierce insistence on being a principal wife had vanished completely, although inwardly she still resented becoming a concubine.

zh: 于是七姑奶奶便要从正面来谈了，“那么，做了小就不要紧了。”她问“不是不要紧，是要做了小，就是说肯拿辛金当夫星，然后才能谈得到前面那四个字的好处。”“你是说，年上月上那四个字？”“是啊！土生金好比母子，木既嫁了金，就是一家眷属，没有再克的道理……”“吴先生，”七姑奶奶打断他的话说：“我是问那四个字的好处。”“好处说不尽。这个八字顶好的是已火那个‘食神’，八字不管男女，有食神一定聪明漂亮。食神足我所生，食神生己、未两土之财，财生辛官，这就是帮夫运。换句话说，夫星显耀，全靠我生的这个食神。”“高明，高明。”七姑奶奶转脸说道：“四姐，你还有什么话要请教吴先生。”
en: The Seventh Lady now turned to the favourable side. “Then she will be all right if she becomes a concubine?” “It is not merely a matter of being all right. Only by becoming a concubine—that is, by accepting xin-Metal as her Husband Star—can we begin to discuss the benefits of those four characters at the beginning.” “You mean the four characters of the year and month pillars?” “Yes. Earth generating Metal is like a mother and child. Once Wood has married Metal, they belong to the same family. There is no reason for further conflict…” “Mr Wu,” the Seventh Lady interrupted, “I was asking about the benefits of those four characters.” “They are endless. The finest feature of this horoscope is the Food God represented by si-Fire. In a horoscope, male or female, the Food God always means intelligence and good looks. It is what the self produces. Here the Food God generates Wealth in the two Earth signs, ji and wei; Wealth generates the xin-Officer. That is the fortune of a woman who advances her husband. In other words, the brilliance of the Husband Star depends entirely on this Food God that she produces.” “Most enlightening!” The Seventh Lady turned to Luo. “Sister Luo, is there anything else you would like to ask Mr Wu?”

zh: 罗四姐迟疑了一下，使个眼色，七姑奶奶知道她要说悄悄话，随即起身走向一边，罗四姐低声说道：“七姐，你倒问他，哪种命跟我合得来的。”“我晓得。”七姑奶奶回到座位上问道：“ 吴先生，如果要嫁，哪种命的人最好？”“自然是金命。”“土命呢？”说着，七姑奶奶微示眼色。吴铁口机变极快，应声而答：“土生金更好。”“喔。”七姑奶奶无所措意似地应声，然后转脸问道：“四姐，还有啥要问？”“一时也想不起。”说这话就表示她已经相信吴铁口是“铁口”，而且要问的心事还多。七姑奶奶觉得到此为止，自己的设计，至少已有七，八分把握，应该适可而止，便招招手叫小大姐将拜金递上来，预备取银票付润金。
en: Luo hesitated, then gave her a look. Understanding that she wanted a private word, the Seventh Lady rose and went aside with her. Luo whispered, “Seventh Sister, ask him what sort of destiny would suit mine.” “I understand.” Returning to her seat, the Seventh Lady asked, “If she marries, Mr Wu, what sort of destiny should the man have?” “Metal, naturally.” “What about Earth?” She gave him the faintest signal with her eyes. Wu was extremely quick-witted. “Earth generates Metal. Better still,” he replied at once. “Oh.” She sounded as though she attached no particular importance to it, then turned to Luo. “Anything else?” “Nothing comes to mind just now.” That answer showed that Luo already believed Wu's pronouncements to be infallible, and that she had much more on her mind to ask him. The Seventh Lady felt that her plan now had at least a seventy or eighty per cent chance of success. It was time to stop. She beckoned her maid to bring her purse, preparing to take out a banknote to pay his fee.

zh: “吴先生，今天真谢谢你，不过还要请你费心，细批一个终身。”“这……”吴铁口面有难色，“这怕一时没有工夫。”“你少吃两顿花酒，工夫就有了。”吴铁口笑了，“这也是我命里注定的。”他半开玩笑地说：“ ‘满路桃花’的命，不吃花酒，就要赴阎罗王的席，划不来。”“哼！”六姑奶奶撇撇嘴，作个不屑的神情，接着说道：“我也知道你忙，慢一点倒不要紧，批一定要批得仔细。”“只要不限辰光，‘慢工出细货’一定的道理。”“那好。”七姑奶奶一面捡银票，一面问道：“吴先生该酬谢多少？”“古太太，你知道我这里的规矩的，全靠托贵人的福，命不好，多送我也不算，命好，我又不好意思多要，随古太太打发好了，总归不会让我白送的。”“白送变成‘送命’了。”七姑奶奶取了一张五十两银票，放在桌上说道：“吴先生，你不要嫌少。”“少是少了一点。不过，我决不嫌。”“我也晓得依罗四姐的八字，送这点钱是不够的。好在总还有来请教你的时候，将来补报。”
en: “Thank you very much for today, Mr Wu. But I must trouble you to write out a detailed reading of her whole life.” “Well…” Wu looked reluctant. “I am afraid I may not have time just now.” “Miss a couple of dinners with courtesans, and you will have time.” He laughed. “That too is ordained by my destiny. With peach blossoms all along my path, if I don't dine with courtesans, I shall have to dine with the King of Hell. It would be a poor bargain.” He was half joking. The Seventh Lady pursed her lips in disdain. “I know you are busy. A delay doesn't matter, but the reading must be very thorough.” “As long as there is no time limit, careful work is certain to produce a fine result.” “Good.” Sorting through her banknotes, she asked, “How much should we pay you?” “You know my rules, Mrs Gu. I depend entirely on the good fortune of my distinguished clients. If a destiny is bad, I won't read it however much I am offered. If it is good, I am too embarrassed to ask much. Give whatever you please. You would never let me give my work away.” “Giving away a destiny would be giving away a life!” She laid a fifty-tael note on the desk. “I hope you won't think it too little.” “It is a little on the low side. But I certainly shan't object.” “I know that for a horoscope like Sister Luo's, this is not enough. We are bound to consult you again. We shall make it up to you later.”

zh: 告辞出门，七姑奶奶邀罗四姐去吃大菜、看东洋戏法。罗四姐托辞头疼，一定要回家。七姑奶奶心里明白，吴铁口的那番斩钉截铁的论断，已勾起了她无穷的心事，要回去好好细想，因而并不坚邀，一起坐上她家的马车，到家以后，关照车夫送罗四姐回去。到了晚上十点多钟，古应春与胡雪岩相偕从宝善街妓家应酬而回。胡雪岩知道七姑奶奶这天陪罗四姐去算命，是特为来听消息的。“这个吴铁口，实在有点本事。说得连我都相信了。”要说罗四姐非“做小”不可，原是七姑奶奶对吴铁口的要求，自己编造的假话，出于他人之口，居然信其为真，这吴铁口的一套说法，必是其妙无比。这就不但胡雪岩，连古应春亦要先闻为快了。“想起来都要好笑。吴铁口的话很不客气，开口克夫，闭口做小，罗四姐动真气了。哪知到头来，你们晓得怎么样？”“你不要问了。”古应春说，“只管你讲就是。”“到头来，她私底下要我问吴铁口，应该配什么命好？吴铁口说，自然是金命。我说土命呢？”七姑奶奶说：“这种地方就真要佩服吴铁口，他懂我的意思倒不稀奇，厉害的是脱口而出，说土生金，更加好。”“小爷叔，”古应春笑道：“看起来要好事成双了。”“都靠七姐成全。”胡雪岩笑嘻嘻地答说。“你听见了？”古应春对他妻子说：“一切都要看你的了。”
en: As they took their leave, the Seventh Lady invited Luo to have a Western meal and watch Japanese conjuring tricks. Luo pleaded a headache and insisted on going home. Her friend understood: Wu's categorical pronouncements had stirred up endless thoughts, and Luo wanted to consider them privately. She did not press the invitation. They rode together in the Gu carriage, and on reaching her own house she told the coachman to take Luo home. After ten that evening, Gu Yingchun and Hu Xueyan returned together from an engagement at a courtesan's house in Baoshan Street. Knowing that the Seventh Lady had taken Luo to have her fortune told that day, Hu had come expressly for the news. “This Wu Tiekou really has some ability. He made even me believe him.” It was the Seventh Lady herself who had instructed him to say that Luo must become a concubine. If she could accept her own invention as truth when she heard it from someone else, his argument must have been extraordinary. Gu was now as eager as Hu to hear it. “It makes me laugh to think of it. Wu was most blunt. Every other word was either ‘bring death to your husband’ or ‘become a concubine.’ Sister Luo was truly angry. But do you know what happened in the end?” “Don't ask us,” Gu said. “Just tell the story.” “In the end she privately asked me to find out what destiny would make a good match for her. Wu said Metal, naturally. I asked, ‘What about Earth?’ That is where I really admire him. It was nothing remarkable that he understood my meaning; what was clever was his instant answer: ‘Earth generates Metal. Better still.’” “Little Uncle,” Gu said with a smile, “it looks as though happy events will come in pairs.” “It all depends on Seventh Sister's help,” Hu replied, beaming. “Did you hear?” Gu said to his wife. “Everything is in your hands.”

zh: “事情包在我身上！不过急不得。罗四姐的心思，比哪个都灵，如果拔出苗头来，当我们在骗她，那一来，她什么话都听不进去了。所以，这件事我要等她来跟我谈，不能我跟她去谈，不然，只怕会露马脚。”“说得不错。”胡雪岩深深点头，“我不急。”“既然不急，小爷叔索性先回杭州，甩她一甩，事情反倒会快。”胡雪岩略想一想答说：“我回杭州，过了节再来。”“对！”七姑奶奶又说：“小爷叔，你不妨先预备起来，先禀告老太太。”“老太太也晓得罗四姐的，一定会答应。”“婶娘呢？”“她原说过的，要寻一个帮手。”“小爷叔，你一定要说好。”七姑奶奶郑重叮嘱，“如果婶娘不赞成，这件事我不会做的。多年的交情，为此生意见，我划不来。”七姑奶奶能跟胡家上下都处得极好，而且深受尊敬，就因为在这些有出入的事情上，极有分寸。胡雪岩并不嫌她的话率直，保证跟婶娘说实话，决不会害她将来为难。“即么，我等你的信。”“好的。我大概过三、四天就要走了。”胡雪岩说：“你看，我要不要再跟她见一次面？”“怎么不要？不要说一次，你天天去看她也不要紧。不过千万不要提算命的话。”一直不大开口的古应春提醒他妻子说：“ ‘满饭好吃，满话难说’。你也不要自以为有十足的把握。如果罗四姐对她的终身，真的有什么打算，一定也急于想跟你商量，不过，她不好意思移蹲就教，应该你去看她，这才是体谅朋友的道理。”
en: “Leave it to me! But we must not rush. Sister Luo is shrewder than anyone. If she detects a clue and decides we are deceiving her, she will refuse to listen to another word. I must wait for her to speak to me about it. If I raise it myself, I may give the game away.” “Quite right.” Hu nodded earnestly. “I am in no hurry.” “In that case, Little Uncle, you might as well return to Hangzhou first. Leave her alone for a while, and things may move faster.” Hu thought briefly. “I shall go back and return after the festival.” “Good. You can make some preparations there. Tell your mother first.” “She knows Sister Luo too. She is sure to agree.” “And Aunt?” “She has said herself that she needs someone to help her.” “You must make quite sure of her agreement,” the Seventh Lady urged solemnly. “If Aunt disapproves, I shan't arrange this. I have known her for years. It would not be worth creating ill feeling between us.” The Seventh Lady got on extremely well with everyone in Hu's household and was deeply respected because she knew exactly how to conduct herself in such delicate matters. Hu did not resent her frankness. He promised to tell his wife the truth and never leave the Seventh Lady in an awkward position later. “Then I shall wait for your letter.” “Good. I expect to leave in three or four days. Do you think I ought to see her again first?” “Of course. You can visit her every day if you like. Only be sure not to mention the fortune-telling.” Gu, who had said little, reminded his wife, “A full bowl of rice is easily eaten; a sweeping promise is hard to fulfil. Don't imagine you are absolutely certain. If Sister Luo really has plans for her future, she must be anxious to discuss them with you. But she may be embarrassed to come seeking your advice. You ought to visit her. That is how to show consideration for a friend.”

zh: 七姑奶奶欣然接受了丈夫的建议，第二天上午坐车去看罗四姐，到得那里，已经十点多钟，只见客堂中还坐着好些绣户。却只有老马一个人在应付。“你们东家呢？”“说身子不舒服，没有下楼。”老马苦笑着说：“我一个人在抓瞎。”“我来帮忙。”七姑奶奶在罗四姐平日所坐的位子上坐了下来，来过几次。也曾参与其事，发料发钱、验收货色，还不算外行。有疑难之处，唤小大姐上楼问清楚了再发落。不过半个钟头，便已毕事。“我上楼去看看。”七姑奶奶问小大姐：“哪里不舒服？”“不是身子不舒服。”小大姐悄悄说道：“我们奶奶昨天哭了一晚上，眼睛都哭肿了。”七姑奶奶大吃一惊，急急问道：“是啥缘故？”“不晓得，我也不敢问。”七姑奶奶也就不再多说，撩起裙幅上楼，只见罗四姐卧室中一片漆黑。心知她是眼睛红肿畏光，便站住了脚，这时帐子中有声音了。
en: The Seventh Lady willingly accepted her husband's suggestion and drove over the following morning. It was already after ten when she arrived. Quite a few embroidery workers were still sitting in the reception room, but Old Ma alone was attending to them. “Where is your mistress?” “She says she is unwell and hasn't come downstairs.” Old Ma smiled helplessly. “I am all at sea on my own.” “I shall help.” The Seventh Lady sat in Luo's usual place. Having visited several times and taken a hand before, she was not entirely unfamiliar with issuing materials and payments and inspecting finished work. Whenever a difficulty arose, she sent the maid upstairs to ask before deciding. Everything was settled within half an hour. “I shall go up and see her. What is wrong with her?” she asked the maid. “She is not ill,” the girl whispered. “She cried all last night, until her eyes were swollen.” Startled, the Seventh Lady asked quickly, “Why?” “I don't know. I didn't dare ask.” She said no more, lifted her skirt and went upstairs. Luo's bedroom was completely dark. Guessing that the light hurt her red, swollen eyes, she stopped in the doorway. A voice came from behind the bed curtains.

zh: “是不是七姐？”“是啊！”“七姐：你不要动。等我起来扶你。”“不要，不要！我已经有点看得清楚了。”七姑奶奶扶着门框，慢慢举步。“当心，当心！”罗四姐已经起来，拉开窗帘一角，让光线透入，自己却背过身去，“七姐，多亏你来。不然老马一个人真正弄不过来。”“你怕光。”七姑奶奶说，“仍旧回到帐子里去吧！”罗四姐原是如此打算，不独畏光，也不愿让七姑奶奶看到她哭肿了眼睛，于是答应一声，仍旧上床，指挥接续而至的小大姐倒茶、预备午饭。“你不必操心。我来了也象回到家里一佯，要吃啥会交代他们的。”七姑奶奶在床前一张春凳上坐了下来，悄声说道：“到底为啥罗？”“心里难过。”“有啥放下开的心事？”罗四姐不作声，七姑奶奶也就不必再往下问，探手入帐去，摸她的脸，发觉她一双眼睛肿得有杏子般大，而且泪痕犹在。“你不能再哭了！”七姑奶奶用责备的语气说：“女人家就靠一双眼睛，身子要自己爱惜，哭瞎了怎么得了！”“哪里就会哭瞎了？”罗四姐顾而言他地问：“七姐，你从哪里来？”“从家里来。”七姑奶奶喊小大姐：“你去倒盆热水，拿条新手中来，最好是新的绒布。”这是为了替罗四姐热敷消肿。七姑奶奶一面动手，一面说话，说胡雪岩要回杭州去过节，就在这两三天要为他饯行，约罗四姐一起来吃饭。
en: “Is that Seventh Sister?” “Yes.” “Don't move. Let me get up and help you.” “No, no. I can see a little now.” Holding the doorframe, the Seventh Lady advanced slowly. “Be careful!” Luo was already up. She drew back a corner of the window curtain to let in some light, then turned her own face away. “Thank goodness you came. Old Ma really couldn't manage by himself.” “The light hurts your eyes. Go back behind your bed curtains.” That was what Luo had intended. Besides finding the light painful, she did not want her friend to see how swollen her eyes were. She agreed and returned to bed, telling the maid, who had followed them up, to bring tea and prepare lunch. “Don't trouble yourself. I feel as much at home here as in my own house. If I want anything, I shall tell them.” Sitting on a bench beside the bed, the Seventh Lady asked quietly, “What is the matter?” “I feel miserable.” “What is it that you cannot put aside?” Luo said nothing, and there was no need to ask further. Reaching through the curtains to touch her face, the Seventh Lady found her eyes swollen to the size of apricots, with traces of tears still on her cheeks. “You must stop crying,” she scolded. “A woman's eyes are everything to her. You must look after yourself. What if you cry yourself blind?” “How could I cry myself blind?” Changing the subject, Luo asked, “Where have you come from?” “Home.” The Seventh Lady called to the maid. “Bring a basin of hot water and a fresh towel—new flannel would be best.” She wanted to apply a hot compress to reduce the swelling. While doing so, she told Luo that Hu would soon return to Hangzhou for the festival. They would give him a farewell dinner in the next two or three days, and she wanted Luo to come.

zh: “哪一天？”“总要等你眼睛消了肿，能够出门的时候。”“这也不过一两天事。”“那么，就定在大后天好了。”七姑奶奶又说：“你早点来！早点吃完了，我请你会看戏。”“我晓得了。”刚说得这一句，自鸣钟响了，罗四姐默数着是十二下，“我的钟慢，中午已经过了。”接着便叫小大姐：“你到馆子里去催一催，菜应该送来了。”“已经送来了。”“那你怎么不开口，菜冷了，还好吃？”罗四姐接着便骂小大姐。七姑奶奶在一旁解劝，说生了气虚火上升，对眼睛不好。罗四姐方始住口。“你把饭开到楼上来。”七姑奶奶关照，“我陪你们奶奶一起吃。”等把饭开了上来，罗四姐也起来了，不过仍旧背光而坐，始终不让七姑奶奶看到她的那双眼睛。““你到底是为啥伤心？”七姑奶奶说：“我看你也是蛮爽快的人，想不到也会这样想不开。”“不是想不开，是怨自己命苦。”“你这样的八字，还说命苦？”“怎么不苦。七姐，你倒想，不是守寡，就要做小。我越想越不服气！我倒偏要跟命强一强。““你的气好象还没有消，算了，算了。后天我请你看戏消消气。”
en: “On what day?” “We must wait until the swelling has gone down and you can go out.” “That will only take a day or two.” “Then let us make it three days from today. Come early. We can eat early, and afterwards I shall take you to the theatre.” “All right.” Just then the clock began to strike. Luo silently counted twelve. “My clock is slow. It is already past noon.” She called to the maid, “Go and hurry the restaurant. The food should have arrived.” “It has.” “Then why didn't you say so? Will it be any good once it is cold?” She began scolding the maid. The Seventh Lady intervened, saying that anger would make deficient fire rise and harm her eyes. Only then did Luo stop. “Bring lunch upstairs,” the Seventh Lady instructed. “I shall eat with your mistress.” When the meal was brought up, Luo got out of bed, but still sat with her back to the light, never allowing her friend to see her eyes. “What has upset you so much? I thought you were a very straightforward person. I never imagined you could brood like this.” “It is not brooding. I resent my miserable fate.” “With a horoscope like yours, you call your fate miserable?” “How can I not? Think, Seventh Sister: either I remain a widow or I become a concubine. The more I think about it, the less I can accept it. I am determined to defy my fate.” “You still seem angry. Let it go. I shall take you to the theatre the day after tomorrow to cheer you up.”

zh: “戏我倒不想看，不过，我一定会早去。”“只要你早来就好。看不看戏到时候再说。”七姑奶奶问道：“小爷叔回杭州，你要不要带信带东西？”“方便不方便？”“当然方便。他又有人，又有船。”七姑奶奶答说：“船是他们局子里的差船，用小火轮拖的，又快，又稳当。”罗四姐点点头，不提她是否带信带物，却问到胡雪岩的“局子”。七姑奶奶便为她细谈“西征”的“上海转运局”。“克复你们杭州的左大人，你总晓得罗？”“晓得。”“左大人现在陕西、甘肃当总督，带了好几万军队在那里打仗，那里地方苦得很，都靠后路粮台接济，小爷叔管了顶要紧的一个，就是‘上海转运局’。”“运点啥呢？”“啥都运。顶要紧的是枪炮，左大人打胜仗，全靠小爷叔替他在上海买西洋的枪炮。”“还有呢？”“多哩！”七姑奶奶屈着手指说：“军装、粮食、药……”“药也要运了去？”罗四姐打岔问说。“怎么不要？尤其是夏天，藿香正气丸、辟瘟丹，一运就是几百上千箱。”
en: “I don't particularly want to see a play. But I shall certainly come early.” “As long as you do. We can decide about the theatre then. With Little Uncle going to Hangzhou, would you like him to take a letter or anything else?” “Would it be convenient?” “Of course. He has servants and a boat. It belongs to his bureau and is towed by a small steamer, so it is fast and steady.” Luo nodded. Instead of saying whether she had anything to send, she asked about Hu's bureau. The Seventh Lady explained the Shanghai Transport Bureau that served the western campaign. “You know Lord Zuo, who recovered your Hangzhou?” “Yes.” “He is now Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu, with tens of thousands of troops fighting there. Conditions are very harsh. They depend entirely on the rear commissariats for supplies. Little Uncle manages one of the most important, the Shanghai Transport Bureau.” “What does it send?” “Everything. The most important things are guns and cannon. Lord Zuo's victories depend entirely on the Western weapons Little Uncle buys for him in Shanghai.” “What else?” “A great deal.” The Seventh Lady counted on her fingers. “Uniforms, food, medicines…” “Medicines have to be sent too?” Luo interrupted. “Of course. Especially in summer. Huoxiang Zhengqi Pills and Biwen Dan are sent by the hundreds and thousands of cases.”

zh: “怪不得。”罗四姐恍然有悟。“怎么？”“那天他同我谈，说要开药店。原来‘肥水不落外人田’。”“肥水不落外人田的生意还多。不过，他也不敢放手去做。”“为啥？”罗四姐问。“要帮手。没有帮手怎么做？”“七姐夫不是一等一的帮手？”“那是外头的。内里还要个好帮手。”七姑奶奶举例以明，“譬如说，端午节到了，光是送节礼，就要花多少心思，上到京里的王公大老棺，下到穷亲戚，这一张单子开出来吓坏人。漏了一个得罪人，送得轻了也得罪。”“送得重了也要得罪人。”罗四姐说，“而且得罪的怕还不止一个。”“一点不错。”七姑奶奶没有再说下去。
en: “No wonder!” Luo suddenly understood. “What?” “He told me the other day that he wanted to open a medicine shop. So the rich water is not to flow into someone else's fields.” “There are plenty of other businesses where he could keep the profits in his own hands. But he doesn't dare give them free rein.” “Why?” “He needs people to help him. How can he manage without them?” “Isn't Brother-in-Law Gu a first-rate assistant?” “In outside affairs. He needs a good assistant at home too.” The Seventh Lady gave an example. “Take the coming Dragon Boat Festival. Think of the trouble involved in sending the gifts alone. From princes and great officials in Beijing down to poor relations, the list is enough to frighten you. Leave one person out, and you offend them. Give too little, and you offend them too.” “Give too much, and you can also cause offence,” Luo said. “And perhaps offend more than one person.” “Exactly.” The Seventh Lady said no more.

zh: 到了为胡雪岩饯行的那一天，七姑奶奶刚吃过午饭，罗四姐就到了。一到便问：“七姐，你有没有工夫？”“啥事情？”“有工夫，我想请七姐陪我去买带到杭州的东西。还有，我想请人替我写封家信。”七站奶奶心想，现成有老马在，家信为什么要另外请人来写？显见得其中另有道理。当时便不提购物，只淡写信。“你要寻怎样的人替你写信？”“顶好是……”罗四姐说：“象七姐你这样的人。”“我肚子里这点墨水，不见得比你多，你写不来信，我也写不来。”七姑奶奶想了一下说：“这样，买东西就不必你亲自去了，要买啥你说了我叫人去办。写信，应春就要回来了，我来抓他的差。”“这样也好。”于是，七姑奶奶把她的管家阿福叫了来，由罗四姐关照，吃的、用的，凡是上海的洋广杂货，在内地都算难得的珍贵之物，以至于阿福不能不找纸笔来开单子。“多谢管家。”罗四姐取出一张五十两的银票，刚要递过去，便让七姑奶奶拦住了。“不必，我有折子。”罗四姐说。阿福不肯接，要看主妇的意思。七姑奶奶已猜到她所说的那个取货的折子，必是胡雪岩所送。既然她不肯用，又不愿要别人送，那就不必勉强了。“好了，随你。”有她这句话，阿福才接了银票去采办。
en: On the day of Hu's farewell dinner, Luo arrived just after the Seventh Lady had finished lunch. “Have you any time to spare?” she asked at once. “What is it?” “If you have, I should like you to come with me to buy things to send to Hangzhou. And I want someone to write a letter home for me.” Old Ma was readily available, the Seventh Lady thought. Why did Luo want someone else to write her letter? Plainly there was a reason. She said nothing about shopping and asked only about the letter. “What sort of person are you looking for?” “Preferably…” Luo hesitated. “Someone like you.” “I have hardly more learning than you. If you cannot write a letter, neither can I.” She thought for a moment. “There is no need for you to go shopping yourself. Tell me what you want, and I shall send someone. Yingchun will be home soon. I shall press him into service to write the letter.” “That will do.” The Seventh Lady summoned her steward, A’fu, and Luo gave him her instructions. Foodstuffs and household articles, all the foreign and southern merchandise sold in Shanghai, were rare and precious in the interior. The list grew so long that A’fu had to fetch paper and brush. “Thank you, steward.” Luo took out a fifty-tael banknote, but as she was about to hand it over, the Seventh Lady stopped her. “There is no need. I have a shop account book,” Luo said. A’fu would not take the money without his mistress's permission. The Seventh Lady guessed that the account book for collecting goods must have been a gift from Hu. Since Luo did not wish to use it, or accept presents from anyone else, there was no reason to insist. “Very well. As you wish.” Only then did A’fu accept the note and go to make the purchases.

zh: 恰好古应春亦已回家，稍微休息一下，便让七姑奶奶“抓差”，为罗四姐写家信。“这桩差使不大好办。”古应春笑道：“是象测字先生替人写家信，你说一句我写一句呢？还是你把大意告诉我，我写好了给你看，不对再改。”“哪种方便？”“当然是说一句写一句来得方便。”“那么，我们照方便的做。”“好！你请过来。”到得书房里，古应春铺纸吮笔，先写下一句：“母亲大人膝下敬禀者”，然后抬眼看着坐在书桌对面的罗四姐。“七姐夫，请你告诉我娘，我在上海身子很好，请她不要记挂。她的肝气病好一点没有？药不可以断。我寄五十两银子给她，吃药的钱不可以省。”“嗯，嗯。”古应春写完了问：“还有。”“还有，托人带去洋广杂物一网篮，亲戚家要分送的，请老人家斟酌。糖食等等，千万不可让阿巧多吃……““阿巧是什么人？”古应春问。“是我女儿。”
en: Gu happened to return just then. After a brief rest, his wife conscripted him to write Luo's letter. “This is not an easy assignment,” he said with a smile. “Shall I work like a character-diviner who writes letters for people, putting down each sentence as you dictate it? Or will you give me the general sense, and I shall write it out for you to read and correct?” “Which is easier?” “Taking it down sentence by sentence, naturally.” “Then let us do it the easy way.” “Good. Come with me.” In the study, Gu spread out a sheet of paper and moistened his brush. He first wrote, “Respectfully submitted at the feet of my honoured mother,” then looked up at Luo across the desk. “Brother-in-Law Gu, please tell my mother that I am well in Shanghai and she need not worry. Is her liver-qi trouble any better? She must not stop taking her medicine. I am sending her fifty taels. She must not economize on medicine.” Gu wrote it down. “Yes. What else?” “I am also sending a basket of foreign and southern goods with someone. Will she decide what to distribute among our relatives? She must be sure not to let A’qiao eat too many sweets…” “Who is A’qiao?” “My daughter.”

zh: “托什么人带去要不要写？”“不要。”“好。还有呢？”“还有。”罗四姐想了一下说，“八月节，我回杭州去看她。”“还有？”“接到信马上给我回信。”罗四姐又说：“这封信要请乌先生写。”“古月胡，还是口天吴？”“不是。是乌鸦的乌。”“喔。还有呢？”“没有了。”古应春写完念了一遍，罗四姐表示满意，接下来开信封，他问：“怎么写法？”“请问七姐夫，照规矩应该怎么写？”“照规矩，应该写‘敬烦某某人吉便带交某某人’，下面是‘某某人拜托’。”“光写‘敬烦吉便’可以不可以？”当然可以。古应春是因为她说不必写明托何人带送，特意再问一遍，以便印证。现在可以断定，她是特意不提胡雪岩的名字。何以如此。就颇耐人寻味了。
en: “Should I mention who is bringing the things?” “No.” “Very well. Anything else?” “Yes.” Luo thought for a moment. “I shall go back to Hangzhou to see her at the Mid-Autumn Festival.” “Anything else?” “She must reply as soon as she receives this letter. And she must ask Mr Wu to write the reply.” “Hu, written with ‘ancient’ and ‘moon,’ or Wu, with ‘mouth’ and ‘heaven’?” “Neither. Wu as in ‘crow.’” “I see. Anything else?” “No.” Gu finished and read the letter aloud. Luo was satisfied. When he came to address the envelope, he asked how she wanted it written. “What is the proper form, Brother-in-Law Gu?” “The usual form is, ‘Respectfully troubling So-and-so to deliver this to So-and-so at a convenient opportunity,’ with ‘Entrusted by So-and-so’ below.” “Could we simply write, ‘Respectfully requesting delivery at a convenient opportunity’?” Of course they could. Gu had asked again because she had already said there was no need to identify the bearer, and he wanted confirmation. He could now be certain that she was deliberately avoiding Hu's name. Her reason for doing so was intriguing.

zh: 罗四姐一直到临走时，才说：“胡大先生，我有一封信，一只网篮，费你的心带到杭州，派人送到我家里。”她将信递了过去。“好！东西呢？”“在我这里。”七姑奶奶代为答说。“胡大先生哪天走？”“后天。”“那就不送你了。”罗四姐说。“不客气，不客气。”胡雪岩问：“要带啥回来？”“一时也想不起。”“想起来写信给我。或者告诉七姐。”
en: Only when she was about to leave did Luo speak to Hu. “Mr Hu, I have a letter and a basket. Would you be so kind as to take them to Hangzhou and send someone to deliver them to my family?” She handed him the letter. “Certainly. Where are the things?” “I have them,” the Seventh Lady answered for her. “When are you leaving, Mr Hu?” “The day after tomorrow.” “Then I shan't come to see you off.” “Please don't trouble yourself. What would you like me to bring back?” “Nothing comes to mind just now.” “Write to me if you think of anything. Or tell Seventh Sister.”

zh: 等送罗四姐上了车，七姑奶奶一走进来，迫不及待地问她丈夫：“罗四姐信上写点啥？”“原来是应春的大笔！”胡雪岩略显惊异他说：“怪不得看起来字很熟。”“我做了一回测字先生。”古应春说：“不过，我也很奇怪，这样一封信，平淡无奇，她为什么要托我来写。平常替她写家信的人到哪里去了？”“当然有道理在内。”七姑奶奶追问着，“你快把信里的话告诉我。”那封信，古应春能背得出来，背完了说：“有一点，倒是值得推敲的，她不愿意明说，信和网篮是托小爷叔带去的。”“她有没有说，为啥指明回信要托乌先生写？”“没有。”胡雪岩要问的话，另是一种，“她还有个女儿？”他说：“她没有告诉过我。”“今天就是告诉你了。不过是借应春的嘴。”“啊，啊！”古应春省悟了，“这就是她故意要托我来写信的道理。”
en: Once they had seen Luo into her carriage, the Seventh Lady hurried back inside and asked her husband, “What did she say in her letter?” “So Yingchun wielded the brush!” Hu said, a little surprised. “No wonder the handwriting looked familiar.” “I played the character-diviner for once. But I found it curious too. Why should she ask me to write such an entirely ordinary letter? What has become of whoever normally writes her letters home?” “There is certainly a reason. Tell me what was in it.” Gu could recite the whole letter from memory. When he had done so, he added, “One point is worth considering. She did not want to say explicitly that Little Uncle was bringing the letter and basket.” “Did she explain why she specifically wanted Mr Wu to write the reply?” “No.” Hu's question was different. “She has a daughter? She never told me.” “She has told you today, through Yingchun.” “Ah!” Gu understood. “So that is why she deliberately asked me to write it.”

zh: “道理还多呢！”七姑奶奶接口，“第一，要看小爷叔念不念旧？她娘，小爷叔从前总见过的，如果念旧，就会去看她。”“当然！”胡雪岩说：“我早就想好了，信跟东西亲自送去。过节了，总还要送份礼。”“这样做就对了。”七姑奶奶又说：“小爷叔，她还要试试你，见了她女儿怎么样？”“嗯！”胡雪岩点点头，不置可否。“还有呢？”古应春这天将这三个字说惯，不自觉地滑了出来。“指明信要托乌先生写，是怕测字先生说不清楚，写不出来，马马虎虎漏掉了，只有乌先生靠得住。”胡雪岩觉得她的推断，非常正确，体味了好一会，感叹他说：“这罗四姐的心思真深。”“不光是心思深，还有灵。我说送礼送得轻了得罪入，他说送得重了，也要得罪，而且得罪的不止一个。”七姑奶奶接下来说：“小爷叔，你要不要这个帮手，成功不成功，就看乌先生写信来了。”胡雪岩心领神会，回到杭州先派人去办罗四姐所托之事，同时送了一份丰厚的节礼。然后挑了个空闲的日子，轻装简从，满荷洒洒地去看罗四姐的母亲。胡雪岩仍旧照从前的称呼，称她“罗大娘”，但罗大娘却不大认得出他了，陌生加上受宠若惊，惶恐不安。胡雪岩了解她的心情，跟她先谈罗四姐的近况，慢慢地追叙旧事，这才使得罗大娘的心定了下来。这心一定下来，自然就高兴了，也感动了，不断地表示，以胡雪岩现在的身分，居然降尊纤贵，会去看她，是她想都不敢想的事。
en: “There are other reasons,” the Seventh Lady said. “First, she wants to see whether Little Uncle remembers old ties. You must have met her mother in the old days. If you remember them, you will go and see her.” “Of course. I had already decided to deliver the letter and things myself. With the festival coming, I must take a present too.” “That is the right thing to do. And she wants to test how you react when you see her daughter.” “Mm.” Hu nodded without committing himself. “Anything else?” Gu had used the phrase so often that day that it slipped out unconsciously. “She specified Mr Wu because she was afraid a character-diviner might not explain things clearly or write them properly, and might carelessly leave something out. Only Mr Wu can be relied upon.” Hu thought her reasoning entirely correct. After considering it for a while, he said with feeling, “Sister Luo's mind works very deeply.” “Deeply and quickly. I said that giving too little could cause offence; she said that giving too much could offend more than one person. Little Uncle, if you want this helper, whether the match succeeds will depend on the letter Mr Wu writes.” Hu understood. Back in Hangzhou, he first sent someone to attend to Luo's commission, adding a generous festival gift. Then, on a free day, he dressed simply, took few attendants and went in an easy manner to visit her mother. He addressed her by the old name, Auntie Luo, but she could scarcely recognize him. His unfamiliarity, added to her astonishment at the honour, made her extremely uneasy. Understanding her feelings, he began with news of her daughter, then gradually recalled old times. Only then did Auntie Luo relax. Once at ease, she naturally became both pleased and moved, repeatedly saying that she would never have dared imagine a man in his present position lowering himself to visit her.
